caption: The N75 dual-carriageway bridge over the Black River, just south of the village. The river slips under here on its way down through farmland from the village crossing at Blackcastle. The road bank carries a good mix of Willow, Hawthorn, Blackthorn and rough grassland, all working as a wildlife corridor between the village and the wider countryside (May 2026)

The N75 directional sign on the southern approach, with a beautiful flowering bank of native Gorse in the foreground. Gorse is a year-round nectar source for early bumblebees and a key shelter shrub for ground-nesting birds (May 2026)

A clean view of the Black River sweeping past mature Willow and Alder on its way south of the village. Two of our most valuable native riparian trees, doing exactly what they're meant to do: stabilising the bank, shading the water and providing cover for fish, dippers and otters (May 2026)

The N75 dual carriageway south of the village, kerb and footpath on the left, hard shoulder and verge on the right with Gorse along the boundary. The road sign post in the middle distance marks the turn off for Twomileborris (May 2026)
